column1: # THE COHERENCE STRIDE -- the 29 open items the eighteen published papers state, against what the
#   register says is open.  GENERATED from 69's census by scripts/build_coherence_stride.py; the RULING
#   and OWNER columns are hand-held and are never regenerated.
# ⚑ WHY THIS PHASE EXISTS, AND IT IS NOT A STRATEGIC QUESTION.  r2695, Daryl: "You can't solve problems
#   in a corpus that's stale all over the place.  If the open problems map is not even a genuine list of
#   open problems ... work the list till it's a legitimate list."
#   ⇒ Node 69's census (r7367_69_the_register_census) read 257 paragraphs across the eighteen published
#   papers, every one in full, and found: ** the register's open list and the papers' open list have
#   almost nothing in common. **  Of 29 distinct open items the papers state, ONE is carried by a live
#   row (PO-50), ELEVEN are stated open while every register row that touched them is STRUCK, and
#   SEVENTEEN have never had a row at all.  P18's own frontier, which the paper calls "complete and
#   unfiltered", lists seven: one live row, six struck.  And ELEVEN places the papers contradict each
#   other about whether something is open -- one-state failures in the published corpus, readable today
#   by anyone opening two papers on the site.
# ⛭⛭ THE SHAPE OF THE WORK, AND IT IS SMALLER THAN THE THREE NUMBERS SUGGEST.
#   It is NOT 11 + 11 + 17 pieces of work.  ** It is 29 items, each needing ONE ruling -- is it open? --
#   and then up to three consequences: **
#     ⒜ the REGISTER: the row goes live, stays struck, or is written for the first time;
#     ⒝ the PAPERS: every paper that states it is rewritten to ONE state (the one-state rule: rewritten
#        to the worked claim, never "was open, later resolved");
#     ⒞ the REMAINDER, in r7013's three kinds: a different kind of object is a ROW, the same question at
#        finer resolution is a STATED LIMIT, and a remainder whose discharge is known is an ORDER.
#   ** One item closes completely before the next.  Nothing leaves this list by reclassification. **
# ⛭ THE RULING TEMPLATE FOR A STRUCK ROW, which is the eleven's whole difficulty.
#   A strike is meant to rest on a receipted answer.  So for each: ** does the strike's ground answer the
#   item the papers state, or something adjacent to it? **
#     * ADJACENT -> the row returns LIVE and the paper was right.  (This is the corpus's most-charged
#       class in another dress: a verdict true of what it examined, taken to license a conclusion about
#       something else.)
#     * IT ANSWERS IT -> the PAPER is stale, and is rewritten to the answer.
#   ⌗ And a third outcome the register could not express until r7371: ** the strike stands as a STOPPING
#   RULE, the item is open, and the row returns live WITH ITS BLOCKER NAMED -- data-gated rather than
#   workable. **  PO-50 is already that shape and was carried as plain OPEN; from here a live row whose
#   discharge waits on a measurement says so in its head, so a reader can tell a workable frontier from
#   a data-gated one.
# ⛔ ORDER OF WORK, and the reason is measured rather than tidy.
#   ① THE CONTRADICTIONS FIRST.  All eleven are live-against-live in print -- a reader can meet both
#     halves today -- and fixing one requires ruling its item anyway, so they are not a separate stage.
#   ② P7 FIRST AMONG THE PAPERS.  It is one side of C1, C2, C3, C6 and C8: ** five of the eleven.  One
#     paper's rewrite clears nearly half the contradictions. **
#   ③ P18's FRONTIER TABLE SECOND.  It is what a reader takes as the programme's open list, and C9 is
#     that list omitting items P18 itself states elsewhere.  ** When this phase ends, P18's frontier
#     table and the register's live rows are the SAME LIST. **
#   ④ THEN the seventeen unrowed items get rows, with their objects named.
#   ⑤ THEN the coherence GATE, below, so the drift cannot recur.
# ⛭⛭ WHAT ENDS THE PHASE, AND IT IS AN INSTRUMENT AND NOT A SWEEP.
#   Nothing in the suite asserts that the register's open list matches the papers'.  That is why the
#   drift was invisible until a census was run by hand.  69's extract.py is the instrument; wrapped as a
#   gate it ratchets: ** every open item the papers state has a live row, and every live row is stated
#   open in a paper or is declared infrastructure. **  Until that gate exists, this list is a measurement
#   that will go stale in silence -- which is this corpus's oldest lesson.
# ⌗ THE PHYSICS WAITS AND THE QUALITY WORK DOES NOT.  Every ruling here is a read of receipts, every
#   registration is an act of registration, and every contradiction is a one-state repair in prose.
#   ** None of it requires doing the physics. **  Opening the physics against a false map is what
#   produced this situation, so the map is made true first.  PO-78 and the Lean line run alongside and
#   are not blocked by it.
# ⛭⛭⛭ r7377 — THE ARCHITECTURE WAS ALREADY THERE, AND FINDING IT CHANGES WHAT THIS PHASE DOES.
#   P7 sec:frontiers carries a comment block, Daryl-directed, stating a standing law:
#     ★ "This is the corpus's ONE open-problems section ... every 'open / frontier / incomplete /
#       remains / not yet / deferred' claim elsewhere in the corpus must reference an item here or be
#       struck as a false-open (the result worked elsewhere, the owed reference supplied).  The law's own
#       home is this section together with THE_REGISTER."
#     ★ "THE BINARY — KILL, or a FAMILY MEMBER ... No third option: 'park' is forbidden."
#   ⇒ So the corpus has FOUR artefacts in this architecture, and three of them are live:
#     ① P7 sec:frontiers — three items (the scalar perturbation sector, WORK; the quantum sector and the
#        matter sector, BOUNDARIES).
#     ② THE_OPEN_PROBLEMS_LEDGER.md — eight numbered families, currency-generated and current to r7371,
#        which declares itself "a view of the register, and the register is the single source of truth",
#        and whose view says ** THREE FAMILIES ARE LIVE: family 3 at PO-31, family 8 at PO-23, family 5's
#        live remainder at PO-56 **.
#     ③ THE_REGISTER — which has STRUCK ALL THREE of those rows.
#     ④ THE_PLAN's canonical opens block — deliberately marked "(historical) the r1241 list", so it is
#        NOT a live mirror and is not a defect.  That demotion was done on purpose and is honest.
# ⛔ ** SO THE DEFECT IS NOT THAT THE PROGRAMME LOST ITS OPEN PROBLEMS.  It keeps them in P7's frontiers
#   section and in the ledger's family view, under a standing law.  What drifted is that the register --
#   which the ledger itself declares the single source of truth -- struck the three rows the other two
#   point at, and neither the view nor the list was updated. **  That is the recurring failure named in
#   this corpus's own standing instructions: retire something and leave everything that references it
#   stale.  69's census found it from the papers' end; this is the same defect seen from the maps' end.
# ⌗ AND THE ASYMMETRY THAT DECIDES EACH CASE: the register's strike is the NEWEST statement, but it is not
#   automatically the right one.  Two of the strikes in question are STOPPING RULES or NON-ATTRIBUTION
#   findings rather than answers, and where that is so the row terminated correctly while the ITEM stayed
#   open -- which is r7013 ①, a different kind of object, and therefore a NEW ROW rather than a lifted
#   strike.
# item\tclass\ttitle\tpapers\tregister\tcontradiction\truling\towner

column3: Whether the damping-tail displacement of the inferred tilt is a tension

column7: CLOSED AT r7381 -- RULED OPEN, AND THE PHASE'S FIRST REOPEN.  All three papers state it and all three agree: P15 §diffusion-scale in print, "Not settled, and unchanged by that run: whether a displacement of that size in the inferred tilt is a tension ... what would make it a tension is a constraint on n_s that does not run through the damping tail, which this fit does not supply"; P6 the same; P18's frontier item 7 "a tension only against an independent measure of the tilt".  PO-24's strike (r6801) priced the displacement at +0.0034 +/- 0.0031, one sigma, on a parameter the construction inherits rather than predicts -- which is P15's OWN reason at l.480.  So the strike and the papers agree on every measured fact and differ only in what they conclude from it: the strike concluded there is nothing to adjudicate; the papers conclude the question is unsettled because what would settle it is not in hand.  ⇒ THAT IS PO-86's THIRD OUTCOME, APPLIED FOR THE FIRST TIME: the strike stands as a STOPPING RULE and the item is OPEN, so PO-24 RETURNS LIVE with its blocker named -- and WORKABLE, not data-gated, because P15 l.482 names the routes itself (the low- and mid-l shape, the polarisation spectra, lensing) and those data exist.  Second half, carried by no row until now: P15 l.492, "the magnitude is not robust to a factor of three ... closing that factor is named here as work not done" -- the same question at finer faithfulness, so r7013 (2) as this row's half rather than a row of its own.  Carried forward and not re-run: the Gaussian residual at correlation 1.000000, the tilt's fixed seven-tenths share, the 6.3x window dependence, the shape residual as an upper bound.  ⇒ NO PAPER EDIT IS OWED: the three papers were already coherent with one another and already right, and THE REGISTER WAS THE SOLE STALE ARTEFACT -- the first such case of the phase.

The item as the papers state it is whether the rest of the matter sector follows once the count, the chirality and the family symmetry are forced, and the corpus already answers it: every remaining entry is a choice and the geometry supplies no choices (PO-30's strike, receipted; P8's criterion: a hierarchy must distinguish three seats the geometry makes identical, so it carries exactly the modulus the criterion rejects); and each remaining entry is a dimensionless magnitude, which needs two invariants where the substrate has one (P7 frontier:sm, P17, receipt P17_no_second_scale_on_either_face). A deeper theory supplying them would be a theory of the matter sector; nothing excludes one, and it is not an item this construction carries. P18 CONTRADICTED ITSELF (l.847 'the matter sector's declared boundary' against its frontier's 'the deepest item ... discharged by a generative law exhibited'): repaired, the frontier no longer lists it, sec:derived states where the content is fixed, and 'What is not on this list' carries it beside the mass hierarchy. column3: Where a generation's colourless triple sits; the fifth multiplet
column5: `PO-45` struck r6733 ("each part of the answer is receipted")
column7: RULED r7433 -- THE THIRD OUTCOME: THE STRIKE IS UPHELD, AND THE CONTRADICTION THE ROW WAS FLAGGED FOR IS NOT THERE.  The flag was PO-45's 'the colourless triple is fixed on the ordinary route' against P14 l.964's 'the fifth multiplet is not a consequence the geometry delivers but a projection it does not carry'.  Read against each other in full they agree on every clause: the triple is a doublet plus a singlet and not a three-fold symmetric object (P14, same section: 'the triple wanted is itself a doublet and a singlet rather than three symmetric objects'); its chirality is R=gamma^5, the Clifford element of the cut's normal r_0, which P14 states in those words; and its states sit on no geometric locus.  ** AND THE FIFTH MULTIPLET IS SETTLED, IN THE NEGATIVE, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO IN TERMS: ** l.221 -- 'Hypercharge therefore rests on the same step as the fifth multiplet---AND THAT STEP HAS BEEN TAKEN, IN THE NEGATIVE.'  What l.964 leaves standing is what a SUCCESSOR must supply, and the paper names the kind: 'to introduce structure rather than to re-read what is present.'  ** A DEMAND ON A SUCCESSOR TO INTRODUCE NEW STRUCTURE IS THE BOUNDARY OF A CONSTRUCTION AND NOT AN OPEN PROBLEM INSIDE IT. **  The register rows what this corpus has not answered, not what it has answered negatively; rowing this one would put it in the business of rowing every result whose sign is minus.  ⌗ BUT THE STRIKE'S STATED GROUND IS THE WEAKER OF THE TWO THE PAPER CARRIES, AND IT IS CORRECTED AT THIS REVISION.  PO-45 listed five loci.  P14 has since walked at least six more -- the lift, the horn spans, the Nariai hexad, the second propagating sector, the reassignment three and the fixed axis -- and says of the whole list that 'the enumeration spans five papers and is not a theorem'.  The ground that IS general is the count: two T-values within one R-eigenspace requires that eigenspace to be at least two-dimensional, hence at least four states, while every two-valued datum the stratification carries is a two-state exchange -- so the colourless four is the one object here with a two-dimensional R-eigenspace and the one object carrying the pair.  The count is added to PO-45's strike at this revision, and the enumeration is kept beside it.

column3: The charged collapse and the Cauchy horizon

column7: RULED r7413 -- THE FIRST OUTCOME: BOTH STRIKES CORRECT, THE GAP BETWEEN THEM, SO A NEW ROW `PO-92`.  PO-25 (struck r6843) answered IS THE STATIONARY OBSTRUCTION PRESENT -- no, the interior mass function is p=1 along the shell, the criterion Q^2/2m_tot > a_eq sin chi falls short by three orders on a framework-mass progenitor, threshold a charge-to-mass ratio near 1e-2, and it was never total across the shells.  PO-49 (struck r6913) answered IS THE THIRD REGIME A REGIME -- no, it is the boundary of admissible initial data and its indicator carries no dynamical variable.  NEITHER STRIKE IS REOPENED.  What neither asked is what P3 states: a Cauchy horizon failing to form is inextendibility and NOT a spacelike r=0, so what stands in the horizon's place, and whether a spacelike origin forms behind it, is unrowed.  ALL FIVE PAPERS ARE CURRENT AND COHERENT -- no correction was owed to any of them, which is unusual on this stride and is the reason this is outcome 1 rather than 3 or 4.  P7 and P9 (twice) carry the identical scope phrase 'ordinary interior analysis rather than a frontier of this construction'; P18 lists it in its seven-item frontier table WHILE declining its subject matter, which is correct -- an unfinished list is complete and unfiltered and an item leaves it by being done, never by reclassification.  WHAT IS AT STAKE IS BOUNDED by the papers' own words: the closed-loop reading of the charged case and NOT the result that collapse continues as a cosmology, whose hypotheses name no charge.  The row carries a live termination: if the question is answerable only inside ordinary interior analysis with no CR-specific content, it is an r7013 kind 2 stated limit and the row closes.

column3: The ultraviolet definition of the interacting graviton tower

column7: CLOSED AT r7389 -- RULED OPEN, AND THE RULING CORRECTS THE SECOND HALF OF THIS SEAT'S OWN r7377 RULING.  WHAT STANDS from r7377: PO-23's strike is UPHELD.  That row's object was 'the ultraviolet definition of the mode sums' and its own column-2 condition read 'a definition of the mode sums, or a demonstration that the obstruction is the general one' -- and a definition WAS delivered, the spectral function calibrated against zeta(0)=10 before use continuing the interacting sum to -4/3 exactly.  WHAT DOES NOT STAND: r7377 concluded 'what remains is P10's wording, which is now the odd statement out'.  P10's wording is RIGHT, and this seat had ruled the item from P7's side without reading P10.  P10 read WHOLE at r7389 (2,019 lines, the mandatory final read satisfied by it since the paper needed no edit): it says 'what remains open is one thing, and it is not a category -- and it is the COMPLETION of a definition' (l.1827); 'the one open thing is the ultraviolet definition of the interacting tower's mode sums -- with the renormalised value at the paying dimension unclaimed and the invariant it is the coefficient of unnamed' (l.1836); and decisively, at l.1485, it REFUSES the inference the ruling made: 'a definition that holds at one order of an expansion and is silent at the next is a definition with an order attached, however small the next order is.  This row exists because a predecessor was struck on an inference of just that shape -- a result true where it was computed, read as true where it was wanted -- and a quantity being negligible is not the same as a scheme being specified.'  ⇒ SO THE TWO OBJECTS SHARE A TITLE AND ARE NOT THE SAME: PO-23 asked for a definition and got one; P10 states open the definition's COMPLETION.  That is r7013 (1), so PO-89 is opened and nothing is unstruck.  It opens in three UNLIKE parts: the renormalised value at dimension six (DATA-GATED -- a measurement, the construction taking the horizon's temperature and never its entropy); which invariant the computed -15405/8192 belongs to (BLOCKED ON THE BACKGROUND -- each of three surviving directions alone reproduces the residue after one rescaling, a rank of one making representatives indistinguishable rather than forced, and the count a lower bound so completing the basis can only deepen it); and the nine-level closed forms (WORKABLE -- six fitted and three held out against a discriminating control, not proved from the recoupling algebra, while the parity they carry IS proved by the channel list's mirror symmetry).  ⌗ C1 is therefore NOT a disagreement about a fact: P7 and P10 agree on every computed thing and differ on whether the row's narrow discharge settles P10's wider item.  OWED AND NAMED: P7 l.1937 ('all three are settled, the ultraviolet definition of the mode sums with them') is the over-claiming sentence and is owed a correction in P7's own turn.  P10 NEEDS NO EDIT.  ⌗ THIRD IN THREE REVISIONS after items 1 and 8 -- a correct strike with the paper's item beyond it -- and 91's fifth face is charged on this seat for ruling from P7's report of P10 instead of from P10.

column5: `PO-30` struck. P7 says the crossing "is settled on the field side and on the worldline side": contradiction C2
column7: CLOSED AT r7387 -- RULED OPEN, AND IT COST A WHOLE TURN ON P7 AND BOUGHT A FRONTIER ITEM BACK.  The ruling turned TWICE.  First reading: a STATED LIMIT, on the ground that nothing rests on the through-crossing evolution and that P16 computes a concrete model's approach (temperature and density along the collapse worldline with a nuclear network on them).  Then the MANDATORY whole-paper read found P7's own canon note, in Daryl's words: "OPEN = the crossing's matter DYNAMICS (the 'how'), NOT its unitarity (the 'whether', settled)" -- P7's body contradicting P7's header, the header Daryl-directed.  The limit reading was withdrawn before it was committed.  Then the ledger showed why the item had no home: its FAMILY 1 is titled with the item verbatim, closed at c54.113 on THE WORLDLINE HALF ("there is no worldline crossing to compute") and retired the P7 enumerated item at c54.115 on that closure -- while the family's OWN 'OPEN:' line, in the same entry, still reads "the detailed worldline-and-field dynamics for a concrete model".  A closure on the worldline half does not reach an open line naming a concrete model's dynamics: PO-86's THIRD OUTCOME for the second time.  CONSEQUENCES, all landed: (a) PO-88 opened -- r7013 (1), since PO-30 (the census's column) was struck on the matter content's generative law, a different object, so no row ever carried this one; (b) P7 rewritten to ONE state -- SIX over-claiming sites corrected, the trailing paragraph folded into a NEW enumerated item 4 (frontier:crossing) classed WORK, the section head now reading "of the four below, two are work and two are boundaries", the Daryl-directed comment's count carried forward with its reason, and the paper recompiled clean at 87 pages; (c) the ledger's family 1 brought current and live again.  C2 is therefore NOT a disagreement about a fact: P15 and P7's canon note were right, P7's body was stale, and the item had left the canonical list BY RECLASSIFICATION -- the one move this programme's rules say a list may never shrink by.  DISCHARGED IN FULL AT r7407 (P15) AND r7409 (P5), one paper per turn as ordered.  P15's sentence turned out to be a SELF-CONTRADICTION rather than an over-statement: sec:scope asked for the 'detailed WORLDLINE and field dynamics' while sec:conclusion already states in print that 'the branch point is crossed by continuation, not traversed by a worldline' -- so the paper's own conclusion carried r7387's content and its frontier item contradicted it.  Corrected to the field half, sourced to the paper's own conclusion.  AND P5's CLAUSE WAS THE MIRROR DEFECT, which is the finding worth keeping: where P15 OVER-stated, P5 UNDER-stated -- 'what remains to be checked of such a model is only whether its history reaches the branch point' excluded the field evolution the corpus carries as open.  Both directions of one incoherence, and only a whole-paper read on each separated them; a census column keyed to the over-claiming phrasing could not have seen P5's at all.  P5 fixed in two places: the 'only' scoped to the two requirements with the field half named beside it, and sec:open's pointer moved off 'the dynamics of matter and fields' onto the field half.  C2 is closed and item 8 owes nothing further.

column3: Which exponent the imaginary segment's own field obeys: $\omega=kc_s$, or the substrate field wi
column5: `PO-79` struck r7145 ("the crossing transports the species the vacuum curve supports")
column7: RULED r7415 -- THE THIRD OUTCOME: NOT OPEN, THE PAPER'S OWN GROUND SETTLES IT, STRIKE UPHELD.  PO-79's head frames the exponent question and the species question as ONE -- 'the two exponents the corpus computes are it acting on two species.  Which species' perturbation does the crossing transport?' -- and its r7145 strike answers it: the crossing transports the species the VACUUM CURVE supports, horn 2 (the plasma sound speed) being excluded EMPIRICALLY by the paper's own refit bound, a transfer carrying c_s shifting the spectrum by 2 c_s k |dEta| = 294.45 at the first acoustic peak against a tilt budget of 0.039, a ratio of 7550.  THE STRIKE IS CORRECT AND IS UPHELD.  ** AND P15 CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON IT, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ITEM ACTUALLY FOUND: ** sec:transmission carries the exclusion in print -- 'the sound-speed reading cannot deliver the tilt it would be invoked to carry', some 7.6e3 times the budget -- while sec:what-crosses still says 'Which of the two the segment's own field obeys REMAINS OPEN, and the consequences drawn below are those the SOUND-SPEED READING SUPPORTS'.  The second half is the worse one: the paper rests consequences on the reading its own other section excludes.  One-state failure, live against live, inside one paper.  OWED: the sec:what-crosses clause rewritten to one state -- the horn settled, its ground named as the refit bound, and the figures below quoted as the naive reductio they are rather than as the reading the consequences rest on.  NO NEW ROW.  ** DISCHARGED r7417. **  sec:what-crosses now reads 'The segment's own field is the SUBSTRATE one' with the ground named as empirical rather than geometric -- the refit bound, 7.6e3 times the tilt budget -- and the figures below quoted as the reductio they are.  THREE FURTHER SITES THE CORRECTION EXPOSED, all found by the mandatory final read and none of them in the item as ruled: (a) the freezing-census branch question said it was 'the same question as the exponent above', which no longer holds once the exponent is fixed on EMPIRICAL ground -- a tilt budget bears on which rate enters the kernel, not on which branch of the lap the census runs along -- so it is now a second question of the same KIND with the first's settlement explicitly not carrying to it; (b) the new clause said the sound-speed value is 'the larger of the two', which is BACKWARDS on the rate -- c_s=1/sqrt3 makes the substrate omega=k the larger, and the paper's own 1e-68 at ell=220 checks out as exp(-k c_s |dEta|) with k|dEta| = 267 -- so it is now 'the weaker damping of the two', which is the conservative reading a reductio wants; (c) sec:largescale COMPUTES the exact transmission ratios at omega = k c_s, the rate now settled as NOT the segment's own, and its figures DO survive downstream where sec:what-crosses claimed neither exponent does.  (c) is closed by a scaling and not by a re-run: omega enters the segment only through the product k c_s, so the substrate reading is the same curve read at sqrt3 times the wavenumber, which preserves size, sign and monotone direction identically and NARROWS the spread across ell -- so both readings there stand a fortiori.

column3: The source of the anisotropic spectrum on the expansion leg: "named here as owed and developed i
column5: `PO-75` struck r7243 ("a stated limit and not an order")
column7: RULED r7415 -- THE FIFTH OUTCOME: THE REGISTER'S SILENCE IS CORRECT AND THE ITEM MUST NOT BE ROWED.  PO-75's r7243 strike says it in terms: 'WHAT REMAINS IS A STATED LIMIT AND NOT AN ORDER', reached after cc66 re-examined both remaining conditions rather than inheriting them and showed them UNDISCHARGEABLE rather than merely unmeasured -- the surviving condition being whether the MODEL's projection kernel is the SKY's, which is circular from the same spectrum and another model's answer from outside, so no bounded version of it exists.  That is r7013 kind 2 exactly, and a kind-2 stated limit is the one class PO-86's own discharge clause (amended r7399) says the register MUST NOT row.  ** AND P15'S WORDING IS WHAT IS WRONG, NOT THE REGISTER: ** the paper says the source is 'named here as OWED and developed in neither this paper nor the bead'.  OWED and STATED LIMIT are different kinds -- a stated limit is a boundary the construction declares, not a debt it carries -- and the paper's word invites exactly the row the register is right to withhold.
